First listed 2026-06-05 · episode or wrap

SpaceX's Exploding Capex, AI Addiction Lawsuits, and the Reality of "TokenMaxxing" | The Weekly Wrap

Eisman emphasizes the funding consequences of adding AI to SpaceX, the gap between compelling technology and purchase valuation, and the risk that metered token costs reduce demand. He sees Alphabet's equity offering as a structural financing change, private-fund gates as a liquidity warning, and homebuilder consolidation as potential support for Meritage. The SpaceX capital-intensity comparison and BCRED restrictions are supported by filings; valuation, behavioral and contagion claims remain conditional or unresolved.

How he reasons here

  • Separate technological achievement from shareholder return.
  • Measure capex against revenue and internal cash generation.
  • Judge AI adoption by output and cost rather than token consumption.
  • Distinguish liquidity restrictions from asset credit losses.
